subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the number of ways of forming a committee of 5 members out of 6 Indians and 5 Americans so that the Indians are always in the majority in the committee.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the committees — which compositions give an Indian majority, how each is counted, and how you finish.
insider_note: Indian majority means three cases — 3, 4 or 5 Indians — and the case list carries its own mark before any ⁿCᵣ is evaluated. The case students drop is all five Indians, ⁶C₅·⁵C₀ = 6, and without it 275 replaces 281.

steps.label: List the allowed compositions
steps.margin_note: First mark. In a committee of 5, a majority means 3 or more. So Indians 3, 4 or 5 with Americans 2, 1 or 0.
lines: Committee of 5; Indians in majority means

recall.must_convey: That a majority of 5 is at least 3, so the cases are 5 Indians, 4 Indians with 1 American, or 3 Indians with 2 Americans.
accept: majority in five means three or more Indians so the cases are five and zero, four and one, three and two
three cases, five Indians, four Indians one American, three Indians two Americans
at least three Indians gives three compositions
five lo majority ante three or more Indians, cases five zero, four one, three two
list the cases with three four or five Indians

steps.why: Majority is a comparison, not a fixed number: in a committee of 5 it means at least 3. Turning the word into the three exact compositions is the step that makes the count possible.
common_mistakes: Taking majority as exactly 3 and missing the 4-and-1 and 5-and-0 cases.
Including 2 Indians + 3 Americans — that is an American majority.

steps.label: Count each composition
steps.margin_note: Two marks. ⁶C₅ = 6, ⁶C₄ = 15, ⁶C₃ = 20; ⁵C₀ = 1, ⁵C₁ = 5, ⁵C₂ = 10. Multiply within each case.

recall.must_convey: That each case multiplies the Indian choice by the American choice — 6, 75 and 200.
accept: six C five times five C zero is six, six C four times five C one is seventy five, six C three times five C two is two hundred
multiply Indians by Americans in each case to get six, seventy five and two hundred
the three cases give six, seventy five and two hundred
prathi case lo Indians into Americans, six, seventy five, two hundred
six times one, fifteen times five, twenty times ten

steps.why: Within a case every group of Indians pairs with every group of Americans, so the counts multiply. ⁵C₀ = 1 is a real factor: there is exactly one way to choose zero Americans.
common_mistakes: Writing ⁵C₀ = 0 and losing the all-Indian case.
Adding the two selections inside a case instead of multiplying.
Computing ⁶C₃ as 6·5·4 = 120 without dividing by 3! = 6.

steps.label: Add the cases

recall.must_convey: That the three case counts are added to give 281.
accept: add six, seventy five and two hundred to get two hundred eighty one
the total is two eighty one
adding the cases gives two hundred and eighty one committees
moodu cases add cheste two hundred eighty one
six plus seventy five plus two hundred is two eighty one

steps.why: Committees with different numbers of Indians are different committees, so the cases do not overlap and their sum is the complete count.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the cases instead of adding.
Dropping the 6 from the all-Indian case and answering 275.
